The Iron Gates to the bend at Harsova, where the Danube turns north into the delta and the frontier leaves it for the Dobruja. In 1450 Bulgaria and the Dobruja are provinces and Wallachia beyond the river is a tributary principality, not one — so the river is the frontier. Kilia and the delta are Moldavian until 1484, which is why this stops short of them. Not declared from 1520: after Mohacs the Ottomans are north of the river and the Danube is an interior road.

contested.name: Crimea
contested.note: Annexed by the Russian Federation in March 2014 after the referendum of the 16th; the annexation is recognised by a handful of states and by no UN resolution. The northern edge is the Perekop isthmus and the Syvash, which Natural Earth 50m draws as solid land.

contested.name: Occupied southern and eastern Ukraine
contested.note: The line the front settled on after the winter of 2022 and held, within this data’s resolution, for the three years after it: Luhansk and most of Donetsk, southern Zaporizhzhia, and Kherson east of the Dnipro. Weekly movement is the drawing layer’s business, not this one’s. The eastern edge is the international border and the south-western one is the river.

follows.note: The international border, from the Kharkiv/Luhansk tripoint to the Sea of Azov.
The lower Dnipro, from the mouth to the Kakhovka reservoir opposite Marhanets.

contested.name: Jammu and Kashmir
contested.note: The princely state whose accession in October 1947 both India and Pakistan have claimed in whole ever since, divided in fact by the ceasefire line of 1949 and the Line of Control of 1972. The Chinese-administered parts — Aksai Chin and the Shaksgam tract — are outside the zone, because China is not one of the two claimants named here.

follows.note: Everything China borders here: the 1963 Sino-Pakistani line, the head of the Siachen, and the Line of Actual Control down to the Himachal tripoint.
The Jammu working boundary, from the Punjab tripoint to Chhamb, where the Line of Control begins.
The Wakhan, from the Broghil to the Chinese tripoint.

contested.name: Western Sahara
contested.note: Spain withdrew in November 1975 under the Madrid Accords; Morocco holds the territory west of the berm and the Polisario Front’s republic the strip east of it, and the referendum the UN mission was created for in 1991 has never been held. The northern edge is the 27°40′N parallel of the 1912 Franco-Spanish convention.

follows.note: The eastern and southern boundaries, from the Algerian tripoint round to Cape Blanc.

contested.name: Abyei
contested.note: The Abyei Area as the Permanent Court of Arbitration redrew it in July 2009 — 10°10′N to the north, 27°50′E and 29°00′E on the sides, the 1956 Kordofan/Bahr el Ghazal line to the south — whose referendum, promised for January 2011 by the Comprehensive Peace Agreement, was never held. Contested from South Sudan’s independence in July 2011.
